reason: The observation is half-right and the consequence is wrong. Right: lately.html:622 builds marks = [0, 15, 30, 45] and the fortnight line sits at 14/axisMax; driven at 1440 the dashed line lands at x=321.7 in a 1034px strip while the "15d" label box starts at 347.2 (centre 358.7), and at 768 the edge gap narrows to 15px. Wrong: there is no 15d tick. .strip-axis is a single hairline with no marks on it; .strip-scale is a row of four floating labels. The fortnight rule is the ONLY vertical mark in the strip, so it cannot be misread as one of a series of ticks that does not exist. Wrong again on the reader's task: nobody rules the threshold off this axis. Membership is encoded on the mark itself (.dot.old paints the disc in accent for age >= fortnight, lately.html:619), stated per-dot on hover and focus ("19 days open") and in the aria-label, summarised in the KPI card, restated in the sr paragraph, and interaction-check.mjs:330 already proves the accent marks past the line equal the number the card claims. The seat's own scenario fails on the frames too: the label reads "A fortnight", a word, never a numeral, so there is no 14-versus-15 arithmetic on screen to get wrong, and a 14-day job would sit ON the line with an accent fill, not on the wrong side of it. The frame's ages are 2,3,5,6,9,11,19,23,41 - the nearest mark to the line is 3 days clear. The declared class is right: refinement, nothing is wrong. What is actually wrong in this strip is something the seat walked past: .strip-scale is display:flex; justify-content:space-between, so the labels are distributed by box width, not placed at their values. Even now the "15d" centre prints 14px (0.6 of a day) right of the true 15-day position, and the moment axisMax leaves 45 - it is derived, Math.max(45, ceil((oldest+4)/5)*5) at line 489 - a 60-day job gives axisMax 65 and the four labels still print at 0/33/67/100% while their values sit at 0/23/46/69%. That is a scale label lying about its own position, which is misleading, not refinement.
sharpenedFix: Do not re-rule the axis on fourteens. Two smaller, correct moves. (1) Fix the real bug: position the scale labels by value instead of by flexbox - absolutely place each mark at left: calc(n / axisMax * 100%) with translateX(-50%), clamping the first and last inside the strip - so the row stays honest for any derived axisMax. (2) If separation from 15d is still wanted after that, do it in the marker, not the axis: the fortnight rule already carries its label at top:0, 61px above the scale row, so give it horizontal air by right-aligning "A fortnight" to the left of the rule (span { right: var(--gap-tight); left: auto; text-align: right }), which moves it away from 15d instead of toward it. Ruling on 0/14/28/42 as proposed would be worse on this source: with marks unchanged in their flex row, "42d" would print at the right edge, which is the 45-day position, and "14d"/"28d" would print at the 15/30-day positions - every label a lie, and the fortnight tick a day off in the opposite direction. It also collides a numeric "14d" tick with the "A fortnight" label at the identical x, which is the coincidence the seat was trying to avoid, and it strands 42 short of an axis end that is by contract a multiple of five.
breaks: The proposed 0/14/28/42 fix breaks the derived-axis contract at lately.html:489 and its comment at :492 (axisMax is a multiple of 5, minimum 45, so a fortnight ruling never reaches the end), silently mislabels every tick because .strip-scale places by flex space-between rather than by value, and duplicates the marker it was meant to disambiguate. The sharpened fix touches .strip-scale positioning and the .fortnight span anchor only. After it lands re-measure: audit.mjs for ink-3 label contrast against the composited card and for the type ramp on .t-unit; interaction-check.mjs:227 (oldest job inside its own axis) and :330 (accent marks equal the card's count), neither of which the change should move; and shots at 390 especially, where the strip is 308px and the today/15d labels already sit 67px apart - centred value-placed labels can collide there and may need the first and last clamped or the interior marks thinned. Re-shoot 390/768/1280/1440 in light and dark, plus the partial and quiet states, since the strip renders in all of them.
